q: A station's balance sheet for a month shows opening outstanding Rs 85,000 and month's earnings of Rs 7,70,000. Cash remitted is Rs 6,90,000 and credits accepted by the Accounts Office are Rs 20,000. The closing station outstanding is:

In March a station remits Rs 1,25,000 through CR Notes, but the bank credits received in March amount to only Rs 50,000 (Rs 40,000 is credited on 1 April and Rs 35,000 on 2 April). The Cash-in-Transit at 31 March is:

A TIA traces a day's collections and finds the CR Note was prepared, but the amount does not appear in the cashier's cash book, though it appears in the traffic check sheet. The break in the remittance trail is at:

options.B: The posting on the receipts side of the cashier's cash book, which follows preparation of the CR Note

q: A station balance sheet tallies on both sides at Rs 8,55,000, but the closing outstanding of Rs 1,45,000 includes to-pay parcels of Rs 60,000 lying undelivered for many months. The TIA should:

options.A: Transfer the amount to imprest cash
options.B: Close the inspection because the totals tally
options.C: Age the outstandings, verify the undelivered parcels physically and pursue clearance of the old items
options.D: Write off the to-pay amount at his own level

q: At a UTS location, the TIA begins inspection and wants to verify the cash at the counter. The correct step is to ask the operator to:

options.A: Hand over the private cash register only
options.B: Prepare a fresh CR Note for the whole month
options.C: Close the counter for the day
options.D: Generate an intermediate Terminal Cash Ticket through the Menu and reconcile the counter cash with the Cash Book/CBS position

q: A station has made a few manual refunds during the period since the last inspection, although manual refunds are normally not permitted at stations. The TIA's extent of check for these refunds is:

options.A: 100 percent check since the last inspection
options.B: No check, since refunds are a commercial matter

q: For wharfage correctness on booked parcels at an 'A' class station, the TIA checks the delivery book for:

options.A: 9 days' transactions, of which 5 dates are in consecutive order
options.B: 15 days' transactions, of which 10 dates are consecutive

q: A TIA suspects tampering with station records during a fraud investigation. He is authorised to:

options.A: Only report the matter and take no record
options.B: Impound certain or the whole record under a Seizure Memo
options.C: Destroy the suspect pages after noting them
options.D: Ask the Station Master to rewrite the records

q: Cash remitted by a station on 30 and 31 March is credited by the bank only in April. In the March accounts this difference between the Traffic Book position and the General Books position is explained by:

options.B: Station outstanding
options.C: Cash in Transit, which normally shows a debit balance and is cleared when the bank credit is received

q: The TIA finds CR Notes for which acknowledgments have not been received from the Cash Office. In the inspection report these items are reported in:

options.B: TA.3F

q: Not-admitted debits (local and foreign) and wharfage and demurrage items awaiting regularisation at a station are listed by the TIA in:

options.B: TA.2F

q: Consider the following statements about the station balance sheet: 1. Sundry earnings are shown on the debit side. 2. Imprest cash is shown on both the debit and the credit sides. 3. The closing balance represents cash in hand at the station. Which statements are correct?

options.B: 2 and 3 only

q: Consider the following statements: 1. The station balance sheet is prepared once a month, compulsorily. 2. It is in substance the personal account of the Station Master. 3. A single combined balance sheet is prepared for coaching, goods and luggage together. Which statements are correct?

options.B: 1 and 2 only

q: Consider the following statements about the TIA's check: 1. Every book, register or return inspected is initialled in red ink and dated. 2. The inventory test check is 10 percent, subject to a maximum of 50 entries. 3. For re-weighment, 5 parcel waybills, inward and outward, per month are test-checked for perishable traffic. Which statements are correct?

options.B: 1 and 2 only

q: The daily order for traffic receipts at a station is:

options.A: CR Note, then cashier's cash book (receipts side), then traffic check sheet
options.B: Traffic check sheet, then CR Note, then cashier's cash book
options.C: Cashier's cash book, then traffic check sheet, then CR Note
options.D: Bank credit, then CR Note, then cash book

q: The top sheet of the station inspection report set, called the Station Performance Sheet, is:

options.B: TA.15F

q: Under the Schedule of Inspections, a 'D' class station is inspected:

options.B: Once in six months
options.C: Once every month — twelve inspections in a financial year

q: Which statement about the station balance sheet is NOT correct?

options.A: Earnings of the month are carried on the debit side
options.B: Cash remitted during the month is shown on the credit side
options.C: The opening balance of a month is the closing balance of the previous month
options.D: The closing balance is the cash physically held at the station

q: Which of the following is NOT within the TIA's prescribed check at a station?

options.A: Counting cash on hand and closing the cash book at the start of inspection
options.B: Checking ticket stock and UTS/PRS terminal cash
options.C: Writing off old station outstandings at his own level

q: Assertion (A): A station balance sheet may tally exactly and yet require serious objection by the TIA. Reason (R): Tallying proves only arithmetical agreement; old outstandings within the closing balance still need ageing, verification and clearance.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true
